Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn, net revenue retention, gross revenue retention). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure.
The churned column is a flag, not a dated event: the share of rows flagged is not a churn rate.

Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure.
The cancellation date in this export is when a customer asked to cancel, not when the subscription ended: a subscription keeps paying until its end date (or a scheduled cancellation date).
Some subscriptions are scheduled to cancel after the latest date: they are still paying and are counted until they end.

On a subscription list, MRR is computed by the product from each subscription's price, seats, discount and billing interval, at today's price: expansion, contraction and revenue retention need monthly MRR snapshots and are not computed from it.

review.review_summary: 10 claims checked against the evidence; 4 flagged (2 unsupported, 2 overstated).
gaps: The analysis does not break down churn by segment or plan to understand where retention is weakest. The evidence shows 131 churned customers and 20.1% logo churn overall, but no segment-level or plan-level churn rates.
No trend analysis of MRR or customer count over the 24-month window. The evidence shows the opening and closing MRR bridge but not how MRR or paying customers evolved month-to-month.

No analysis of expansion and contraction patterns by segment or plan. The evidence shows total expansion MRR ($89,367.79) and contraction MRR ($36,744.52) but not which segments or plans drove these movements.
next_investigations: Segment churn by segment and plan to identify which customer cohorts are at highest risk. Compare logo churn rate and churned MRR across Enterprise, Mid, and SMB segments.
Analyze the 131 churned customers by tenure, MRR at churn, and segment to understand whether churn is concentrated in new, small, or specific-segment customers.
Track MRR and customer count trends month-over-month across the 24-month window to identify when growth accelerated or decelerated and whether churn or contraction drove any downturns.
methodology_concerns: Logo churn (20.1%) and the count of churned customers (131) measure different populations: logo churn counts only customers in force on 31 Oct 2025 who are not in force on 31 Oct 2026, while the 131 count includes customers who joined and left within the window. The evidence notes this difference but the report does not clarify which metric applies to which question.

MRR is a snapshot at month-end, not revenue. The evidence states that movements compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over 12 months, and a customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure. This means the churn and retention metrics may undercount short-lived customers.
